The alert followed Iranian attacks on US assets in Bahrain and Kuwait and a Houthi strike on Riyadh that injured 11 people.

items.title: Qatar says it ‘will not accept’ attacks after Iran protests over joint statement with Germany
items.summary: Iran summoned a Qatari diplomat in Tehran over a joint statement with Germany condemning Iranian attacks and threats to shipping. Qatar said it will handle the dispute through diplomacy and that both the US and Iran were still participating in its mediation efforts.

items.title: Violence against women: Its many forms and the paths to justice
items.summary: PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, November 25: Some 21 percent of women say they have suffered "economic violence", while others are exploring new types of justice for their abusers. In other news, recent leaks on Russian troop losses show 349 deaths in Mali, Russia's biggest military deployment in Africa. As Spain prepares to head to the polls, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announces a raft of social measures. Finally, a plucky young cat from Essex has taken a train to London.

items.title: Life expectancy in Cuba falls for first time since 1950 amid economic crisis
items.summary: WHO chief says life expectancy has fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 in 2025, figures that predate US fuel blockade Life expectancy has fallen for the first time in Cuba since 1950 as the island reels from a severe economic crisis, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday. On a visit to Havana, the WHO chief, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, said life expectancy had fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 years in 2025, the first decline since records began in 1950. items.title: Ukraine seeks €115 billion in foreign aid for 2027, Zelensky says
items.summary: Ukraine will need €115 billion in external financing next year to sustain its economy and war effort against Russia, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, adding that Kyiv had secured commitments for about €90 billion from the European Union.

items.title: Australia set to pass online safety laws with multibillion-dollar fines for tech giants
items.summary: The Australian government clinched a political deal on Tuesday to introduce online safety laws that could expose tech giants to multibillion-dollar fines for failing to prevent foreseeable online harms.

items.title: U.S. criticizes Australia social media law as harming free speech

items.title: A Lion on the Loose Near Istanbul? Not So Fast.
items.summary: Blurry surveillance footage spurred a frantic search — until the Turkish authorities said it was unclear whether the animal was the feline.

items.title: Was it a lion? Grainy footage prompted a large search in Istanbul
items.summary: Reports of a lioness roaming north of Istanbul prompted a security scramble after grainy footage appeared to show a large cat prowling across open land. Following a day of searches, Turkish authorities said the animal was neither a lion nor any other big cat.

items.title: High prices force many across the US to scale back for Thanksgiving: ‘We can’t afford the food’
items.summary: Americans are opting for smaller gatherings, reconsidering travel or swapping expensive ingredients for cheaper alternatives Thanksgiving is just one day away, but for some Americans, the holiday may look a little different this year as higher costs for food, drinks , household goods, air travel and gasoline have prompted some families to rethink their plans and spending. The Guardian recently asked readers across the United States how they were marking the holiday this year and whether higher prices had affected their plans or made them rethink their usual traditions. Continue reading...

items.title: Heavy rain and high winds on east coast threaten to disrupt Thanksgiving plans
items.summary: Macy’s parade of balloons under threat in New York City as flights face delays or cancellations Two storms that converged in the US south-east will move up the east coast, potentially disrupting plans for millions of Americans travelling to celebrate Thanksgiving with heavy rain, strong winds and possible flooding from Virginia to New York. Strong winds expected to arrive in the north-east on Thursday could prevent the balloons from flying at the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade in New York, where wind gusts could hit 60mph.
